{"self_assessment": "Impact: I drew the fish body on the scratch pad, with top and bottom curves from the tail end round to the nose. That sketch gave the table its shape, and the rest of the build grew from it. I laid the start domino and traced the top line (stroke 1) from the tail round to the nose. Every other stroke hangs off that run, so it was central to the result. Before the push, my final check showed about 122 of 125 standing dominoes connected to the start, covering the body, both tail lobes and the fin. The only unconnected pieces were three small strays that wouldn't show.

Execution: I built steadily and then spent the second half of the session on verification. I made repeated close inspections of the body, the joints and the fin area. I reported what I found back to the table in plain terms and ran a full check before the push. I also kept my hands off the finished body so nothing got bumped.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed throughout. I asked people to take specific strokes, pointed Tom to a connect from the top line when the fin wouldn't catch, and confirmed joints as they came together. I stayed out of other people's working areas to avoid bumps and crowding.

Leadership: I helped the table settle on a clear plan early, a big, simple fish whose outline reads on its own. I assigned work so people weren't overlapping. As time ran down I called out the countdown, asked everyone to keep their hands off, and kept the mood calm and upbeat. I believe my contribution to the result was substantial, since the body sketch, the start and the top run were the backbone and I ran the final check.", "my_share_percent": 35}
